from.place: Theorem lemma-theorem construction, use of the Baer criterion for injectivity

title: Baer criterion using a generator
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with generator $U$. An object $I$ of $\mathcal A$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions] if and only if for every subobject $M\subset U$, every morphism $M\to I$ extends along $M\hookrightarrow U$ to a morphism $U\to I$.

proof.text: The forward implication is immediate from the definition of an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]: for every monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow N$ every morphism $M\to I$ extends to $N$, in particular for every monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow U$ from a subobject $M\subset U$.

For the converse, fix a monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$ and a morphism $\varphi:A\to I$. Partially order the set $S$ of pairs $(A',\varphi')$ consisting of a subobject $A\subset A'\subset B$ and a morphism $\varphi':A'\to I$ extending $\varphi$, by $(A'_1,\varphi'_1)\le(A'_2,\varphi'_2)$ if $A'_1\subset A'_2$ and $\varphi'_2|_{A'_1}=\varphi'_1$. A totally ordered subset $T\subset S$ has an upper bound: $A'=\operatorname{colim}_{t\in T}A'_t$ with the induced morphism $\operatorname{colim}_t\varphi'_t:A'\to I$. Since filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ are exact (AB5, [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]), the colimit of the monomorphisms $A'_t\hookrightarrow B$ is a monomorphism $A'\hookrightarrow B$, so $A'$ is a subobject of $B$ containing each $A'_t$, and the colimit map restricts to $\varphi'_t$ on each $A'_t$, hence to $\varphi$ on $A$. By Zorn's lemma $S$ has a maximal element $(A',\varphi')$.

source.place: Lemma 19.11.6 (Tag 079G), proof, construction of S and Zorn upper bound

proof.text: Suppose $A'\neq B$. Then the quotient map $B\to B/A'$ is nonzero, so since $U$ is a generator (separator, [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]) there is $\psi:U\to B$ whose composite $U\to B\to B/A'$ is nonzero, i.e. $\psi$ does not factor through $A'\hookrightarrow B$ (this is the generator condition of Stacks Tag 079B). Let $N=A'\cap\operatorname{Im}(\psi)$ and $M=\psi^{-1}(N)\subset U$; then $\psi$ restricts to an epimorphism $M\to N$. By the assumed condition the composite $M\to N\hookrightarrow A'\xrightarrow{\varphi'}I$ extends to a morphism $\chi:U\to I$.

source.place: Lemma 19.11.6 (Tag 079G), proof, choice of psi and definitions of N and M; generator as in Definition 19.11.1 (Tag 079B)

proof.text: Since $\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)=\psi^{-1}(0)\subset M$ and $\chi|_M$ factors through $\psi|_M:M\to N$, we get $\chi|_{\operatorname{Ker}(\psi)}=0$. Hence $\chi$ factors as $U\to\operatorname{Im}(\psi)\xrightarrow{\varphi''}I$. Because $M\to N$ is an epimorphism, $\varphi''$ and $\varphi'$ agree on $N=A'\cap\operatorname{Im}(\psi)$, so they glue to a morphism $A'+\operatorname{Im}(\psi)\to I$ (the sum is the pushout of $A'\leftarrow N\to\operatorname{Im}(\psi)$) extending $\varphi'$, hence $\varphi$. Since $\psi$ does not factor through $A'$, the subobject $A'+\operatorname{Im}(\psi)$ strictly contains $A'$, contradicting maximality.

source.place: Lemma 19.11.6 (Tag 079G), proof, factorization through image and gluing

proof.text: Thus $A'=B$, so $\varphi':B\to I$ extends $\varphi$. Since the monomorphism $A\hookrightarrow B$ and the morphism $\varphi:A\to I$ were arbitrary, $I$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Lemma 19.11.6 (Tag 079G), proof, final contradiction and conclusion
